Use the pre-built `rightsNodesById` Map to perform an O(1) lookup instead of a linear scan (`.find`) inside the loop.

```suggestion
      const rightNode = rightsNodesById.get(to);
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Optimize linear scans in array filtering by mapping lookup keys to a Set beforehand to reduce complexity from O(N * M) to O(N + M), ensuring existing classification behavior is preserved.
</details>

Use the pre-built `receiptByQuestionKey` Map to perform an O(1) lookup instead of a linear scan (`.find`) inside the loop.

```javascript
    const fallbackReceipt = receiptByQuestionKey.get(answerQuestionKey);
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Optimize linear scans in array filtering by mapping lookup keys to a Set beforehand to reduce complexity from O(N * M) to O(N + M), ensuring existing classification behavior is preserved.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

There is a signature mismatch in the call to `toStringValue`. The function only accepts two parameters (`value` and `fallback`), but three arguments are passed here: `toStringValue(methodProps.attempt_loop_target, null, question_ref)`. As a result, the third argument `question_ref` is completely ignored, and if `attempt_loop_target` is null, it falls back to `null` instead of `question_ref`. If the intention is to fall back to `question_ref`, pass it as the second argument.

```suggestion
    attempt_loop_target: toStringValue(methodProps.attempt_loop_target, question_ref),
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Sort the projected rows lexicographically by `question_key` using strict byte-order comparison to prevent diff churn and ensure deterministic ordering across environments.

```suggestion
  const rows = toArray(Array.from(indexes.questionsById.values()))
    .map((question) => buildQuestionRow(question, indexes))
    .sort((a, b) => (a.question_key < b.question_key ? -1 : a.question_key > b.question_key ? 1 : 0));
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Ensure generated JSON arrays are strictly ordered by their ID fields (e.g., using a helper like `sortByIdByteOrder`) to prevent diff churn, and update corresponding test expectations to match this sorted order.
</details>
